summary: Sh. Ali Mashhour discusses the conditions required for prayer (salah) to be valid in Islam. He first reviews the six conditions listed by the author: Islam, covering oneself, intention, purification of body/clothing/place, facing the Qibla, and knowing the prayer time. Sh. Ali Mashhour then introduces three additional conditions not mentioned by the author: being Muslim, being sane (able to hold a coherent intention), and reaching the age of discernment (typically by age seven). Through practical examples—such as a non-Muslim coworker praying in rows and young children in the prayer line—Sh. Ali Mashhour illustrates how these conditions affect the validity and acceptability of salah, emphasizing that Islam is the foundation upon which all good deeds must be built.
suggested_title: The Nine Conditions of Valid Prayer (Salah) in Islam
